title: Misty Harbor: the Wells suite-and-pool weekend that keeps things easy
summary: A full kitchen, separate living space and indoor water can do more for a family weekend than a fashionable lobby. This is the kind of stay where the room can actually function as home base.
search: A photo plan for the day.Choose the destination and make a visual plan you can change.Make our visit plan → Family-tested · Maine coast · OvernightMisty Harbor: the Wells suite-and-pool weekend that keeps things easyWells, MaineA full kitchen, separate living space and indoor water can do more for a family weekend than a fashionable lobby. This is the kind of stay where the room can actually function as home base.60 Mile RdWells¾ mileFrom Wells BeachIndoorPool + hot tubFull kitchensSuite setupEditorial still-life illustration for a day out. from our Maine visitA little room for a Maine weekend.Misty Harbor was our base for a Wells getaway. The pool and the practical shape of the stay belong to the sort of trip we like: time together, a few good stops, and room to come back and settle in.A little plan to beginPlan the pool time first, then decide whether an outing still sounds good.Make our visit planKeep one good thing. Leave room to change your mind. From our family notebook · a Maine overnightThe best part was that nothing had to be a big production.There is a particular kind of relief in opening the door to a hotel room and realizing the room itself is going to help. Not merely look nice in photographs. Help. At Misty Harbor, the useful things were the lovely things: enough space to spread out without living out of a heap of bags, a kitchen that meant dinner did not have to become another outing, and the indoor pool waiting downstairs like a perfectly reasonable answer to the question, “What should we do now?”We have become suspicious of weekends that arrive with too many verbs. Visit. Shop. Tour. Reserve. Hurry. This one worked better because the list was short. We brought in the bags, made the suite feel familiar, found the chargers, put the swim things where we could actually find them again, and went to the water. That was the event. No one needed to earn it by sightseeing first.Wells is good for this kind of trip because Maine is outside the window even when you are not doing Maine particularly hard. The coast is close. There are places to get something easy to eat. You can take a drive, see the water, come back, and still feel as though you went somewhere. A swim can become the center of the afternoon instead of the leftover activity squeezed between adult plans.What we remember is not a checklist of attractions. It is the feeling of everybody having a little room around them. Wet swimsuits could dry. One person could be awake while another was finished with the day. We could make food without negotiating a restaurant. We could go back to the pool because, wonderfully, there was no rule saying the second swim did not count as an itinerary.That is increasingly our definition of a good family hotel: it gives the day somewhere to land. Misty Harbor did. The weekend felt simple, coastal, comfortable and ours—which, for us, is considerably better than impressive.It is the kind of place we would choose again not because it asks to be remembered, but because it leaves room for the family to make the memory. That distinction matters to us more every year. Give us a clean landing place, a pool, a workable kitchen and the freedom to change the plan, and we can supply the rest.Family story, lightly edited from our notes, memory and camera roll.
